nodeType.origin: derived-local: nodeType = type(node).__name__ for the AST node passed to evaluate(); NOT a free public input. Value is supplied by runtime AST traversal position, seeded enum domain {Module, Expr}.
nodeType.note: The seeded enum abstracts the runtime class name of the visited node. Z3 treats it as a free enum const, which is why both witnesses are sat; the real value is fixed by where in the parsed tree the recursion currently is.

encoding.notes: Encoded nodeType as a 2-value Z3 EnumSort matching the seeded domain {Module, Expr}. The predicate is a single string equality. expressionStr (seeded {'a == 1','a + b'}) does NOT appear in the predicate and does not control its truth value: every valid expression string parses to a root ast.Module, so the top-level call is always nodeType=='Module' regardless of expressionStr.

true_examples.note: Top-level call ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate(tree, ctx) where tree is the ast.Module root. Holds identically for expressionStr='a + b' (root is always Module).

false_examples.note: First recursive call evaluate(node.body[0], ...) visits the ast.Expr child -> branch not taken (falls through to the 'Expr' elif at line 634).
Deeper node ('a == 1' -> Compare; 'a + b' -> BinOp). Outside the seeded enum {Module,Expr} but representative of the real false-by-value space; runtime-confirmed, not z3-proven over the 2-value enum.

grid_enumeration.runtime_extension: Real AST traversal also produces Compare, BinOp, BoolOp, UnaryOp, Call, Name, Constant, etc. as nodeType; all are false for this predicate. Only the single root visit is ever True.

pure_helper:
def is_module_node(nodeType: str) -> bool:
    """Mirror of Configuration.py:630 dispatch.
    nodeType = type(node).__name__ for an AST node visited by
    ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate. Returns True iff the node is the root
    ast.Module (the branch taken at line 630). Pure over the string
    nodeType; the real value is supplied by runtime AST traversal, so a
    True/False result here does not characterize any PUBLIC input -- it
    characterizes WHERE in the parsed tree the recursion currently is.

    pre: nodeType in ('Module', 'Expr')
    post: __return__ == (nodeType == 'Module')
    """
    return nodeType == "Module"

crosshair.caveat: Absence of a counterexample from CrossHair is NOT a proof of correctness; it is bounded symbolic exploration over the seeded string enum. The first (no-contract) run reported 'no checkable functions' because the bare helper has no postcondition to refute.

verification.method: Ran ast.parse(expressionStr, mode='exec') in-container for both seeded expressionStr values and read type(node).__name__ at root, body[0], and body[0].value.
verification.consistency: Z3 enum witnesses match runtime: Module reachable only at the root visit (True); Expr reachable at first recursion (False). Both seeded expressionStr values give the identical node-type sequence, confirming expressionStr is not load-bearing for this predicate.

classification_rationale: runtime-dependent. The predicate compares type(node).__name__ against the literal 'Module' -- a nodeType dispatch over a parsed AST tree (exactly the step-3 category: isinstance/nodeType dispatch over a parsed tree). nodeType is a derived-local, not a public input: its value is fixed by the recursion's position in the ast tree, not by any solvable function of CLI/YAML/int/bool inputs. The seeded public input expressionStr does not appear in the predicate and cannot flip it -- ast.parse(any_valid_expr, mode='exec') always yields a root ast.Module, so the top-level call is unconditionally True and the recursive calls are unconditionally False. Z3 produces both witnesses (sat) only because nodeType is modeled as a free enum const; this is an abstraction of runtime state, so solver_status=sat is reported but classification stays runtime-dependent (the truth value is governed by traversal position, not by a static input function). Note: at the sole top-level entry the branch is a structural tautology (always taken once per evaluated expression).
